title: Lever Reviews, Pricing, and Alternatives (July 2026)
summary: Lever ATS costs $6-8 per employee monthly with limited reporting. Read our July 2026 review of Lever pricing, features, and better free alternatives like Dover.
body_markdown:
Researching Lever reviews before committing to an ATS? The polished demo often differs from what teams face once hiring ramps up. Reporting feels narrow, search tools miss context, and pricing can climb fast as headcount or add-ons grow. This guide covers the real benefits, the drawbacks that surface after adoption, and[Lever alternatives](https://www.dover.com/) that may offer stronger workflow control and better long-term value.


**TLDR:**


-


Lever is commonly reported by third-party sites to cost $6-$8 per employee monthly but lacks transparent pricing and requires sales calls.


-


Some users report limitations in search flexibility and reporting customization, particularly when they need highly specialized queries or metrics.


-


Some modern ATS platforms now offer free, unlimited plans with AI résumé scoring and broad job board distribution.


-


Fractional recruiting services from third-party partners often average $2K-$7K per hire, compared to Lever’s software-only approach.


-


Newer solutions combine free recruiting software with optional on-demand vetted recruiters designed for startup budgets.


## Lever Overview: What It Is and How It Works


Lever is a cloud-based[applicant tracking system](https://www.dover.com/blog/best-applicant-tracking-systems-recruitment) that combines ATS functionality with candidate relationship management (CRM) capabilities. Founded in 2012, the company serves growing, midsized, and enterprise organizations looking to manage talent acquisition in one centralized system.


The core differentiator Lever promotes is LeverTRM ([Talent Relationship Management](https://www.aihr.com/blog/talent-relationship-management/) ), which merges traditional applicant tracking with CRM tools for nurturing passive candidates and building talent pools over time. This lets you track active applicants through your hiring funnel while maintaining relationships with prospects who aren’t ready to apply yet.


### How Lever Works


Lever allows recruiting teams to post jobs, collect applications, and move candidates through[customizable hiring stages](https://www.dover.com/blog/startup-ats-guide) . The CRM side lets you source passive candidates, add them to nurture campaigns, and tag them for future opportunities. The system includes interview scheduling, feedback collection, and offer management to handle the full candidate lifecycle.


Hiring managers and interviewers can access candidate profiles, leave feedback, and participate in the decision-making process. Lever also offers analytics dashboards to track recruiting metrics like[time-to-fill](https://www.shrm.org/about/press-room/shrm-releases-2025-benchmarking-reports--how-does-your-organizat) and source effectiveness.


### Pricing Structure


Lever operates on a subscription model with pricing between $6 and $8 per employee per month. However, Lever doesn’t publish set pricing tiers publicly. Certain capabilities are available through different packages or add-ons, so the final cost depends on which capabilities you need and requires going through a sales process to get an accurate quote.


## Lever Features


Lever combines its ATS and CRM into a single candidate database, handling both active applicants and passive prospect relationships. The system includes customizable pipeline stages that adapt to different roles, with automated candidate movement based on triggers you define.


### Automation and Workflow Tools


Automated email campaigns nurture passive candidates through personalized sequences without manual follow-up. Interview scheduling syncs with team calendars and sends confirmations automatically, while résumé parsing extracts candidate data into structured profiles. Standardized feedback forms collect interviewer input across your hiring team.


### Integrations and Analytics


Lever connects with third-party applications, including Slack for candidate updates, BambooHR for new hire transfers, DocuSign for e-signatures, and Tableau for analytics. The reporting dashboard tracks funnel drop-off points, source performance, and hiring velocity. Custom reports let you monitor team-specific KPIs, with workflow customization for approval chains, interview plans, and permission controls.


## Lever Key Limitations and Gaps


Lever’s feature set works well for many teams, but certain constraints surface as organizations scale or require deeper customization.


### Search and Reporting Constraints


Lever supports keyword and[Boolean search](https://libanswers.snhu.edu/faq/8739) alongside candidate filters, although some users may find its available search fields or workflow less flexible than those of competing platforms.


The reporting functionality draws frequent criticism for inflexibility. Lever includes preset analytics dashboards, while custom charts, dashboards, and reports are available through its Data Explorer functionality on eligible packages or with the Advanced Analytics add-on.


### Cost and Integration Gaps


Lever relies on third-party integrations like DocuSign or Adobe Sign for e-signatures, which can add cost and setup time.


The pricing model creates challenges at both ends. Depending on the quoted package and contract, startups may face higher costs for advanced features, integrations, or API access, while longer contract terms may reduce flexibility if hiring needs change.


### Performance at Scale


Some user reviews report slower system performance when candidate volumes increase. Onboarding capabilities remain minimal, requiring manual setup when expanding to new teams or regions.

## A Strong Lever Alternative for Startups


Dover offers a free, unlimited ATS that’s ready to use in minutes with no credit card required. While Lever’s annual costs range from around $3,500 to well over $140,000, Dover includes[AI-powered resume scoring](https://www.dover.com/blog/best-application-scoring-tools-for-recruiters) , job board distribution across major hiring sites, and a Chrome sourcing extension at no cost.


The key difference is Dover’s combination of free recruiting software with access to[fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-a-fractional-recruiter-guide) who work as part of your team. This solves Lever’s limitation of being purely software-focused. Dover’s[fractional recruiting model](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-costs) averages $2K-$7K per hire with complete transparency, eliminating the need to purchase separate ATS software or manage multiple vendor relationships.


For startups, Dover removes the barriers that make Lever prohibitive: high costs, lengthy sales processes, and feature limitations behind paywalls. AI-generated career pages, employee referral tracking, and real-time analytics provide enterprise-level functionality through a startup-friendly approach. Companies like[Stripe, Scale AI, OpenSea, and Vanta](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dover) have used Dover to scale their teams.


In addition, Dover supports teams with tools that help reduce busywork and improve coordination across hiring managers, founders, and recruiters. You gain practical support on outreach tactics, candidate review habits, and interview flow without hiring more internal staff. This setup helps[early-stage companies](https://www.dover.com/blog/dover-vs-lever) maintain flexibility while still moving with speed during active searches. Teams growing across multiple departments can rely on Dover to keep information organized, respond quickly during surges in applications, and maintain clear visibility across each stage of the funnel.


### Other Lever Alternatives


Several long-standing alternatives serve different market segments. Greenhouse offers sophisticated workflow automation and DEI tools for mid-market and enterprise companies, though pricing reaches similar levels as Lever. BreezyHR serves small to mid-sized businesses with subscription plans starting around $143 monthly for basic features. Workable provides all-in-one HR capabilities beyond recruiting for companies seeking broader people management tools.


The right choice depends on your company stage and needs. Enterprise organizations with dedicated recruiting teams might find Lever’s cost workable. Startups looking to hire without breaking the bank will find[Dover’s free ATS](https://www.dover.com/compare/dover-vs-lever) combined with flexible access to vetted recruiters offers the most value.


## Why Dover Works Where Lever Falls Short


Lever’s core limitations come down to two things: cost and capacity. The subscription provides recruiting software, including ATS, CRM, automation, and analytics capabilities, but it does not provide hands-on recruiting personnel when a team needs additional hiring capacity. There’s no built-in access to recruiting help when a search gets difficult, a hiring surge hits, or a founder needs experienced support without adding headcount. Teams end up paying for the software and then figuring out recruiting separately, which adds both expense and coordination overhead.


Dover is built to close that gap. The ATS is free with no seat limits, no job limits, and no credit card required. It handles job posting to over 100 boards,[AI-powered resume scoring](https://www.dover.com/blog/best-application-scoring-tools-for-recruiters) , branded careers pages, employee referral tracking, automated scheduling, and pipeline management in one place. When a search needs more hands-on work, Dover’s recruiter marketplace connects companies with experienced[fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-a-fractional-recruiter-guide) who work inside the same system, keeping candidate data, sourcing notes, and pipeline progress in one shared view. There’s no separate agency relationship to manage and no candidate data walking out the door at the end of a search.


The cost structure is a meaningful shift from Lever’s model. Dover’s fractional recruiting runs $75-$125 per hour with no retainer, and most companies spend[$2,000-$7,000 per hire](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-costs) depending on role complexity. Getting started requires only an $800 refundable deposit, with no long-term contracts. For startups and growing teams that need both reliable software and access to recruiting expertise without committing to a full-time hire, Dover offers a structure that fits how early-stage companies actually operate.


## FAQs


### How much does Lever actually cost compared to free alternatives?


Lever charges $6-$8 per employee per month with annual costs ranging from $3,500 to over $140,000 depending on your team size and features needed. Free alternatives like Dover provide unlimited ATS access, AI résumé scoring, and job board distribution at no cost, with optional fractional recruiting services averaging $2K-$7K per hire. SHRM’s recruiting benchmark puts the 2025 median cost per hire for nonexecutive positions at approximately $1,200, although actual costs vary considerably by role, organization size, and hiring method.


### What’s the main difference between an ATS with CRM features and a recruiting tool?


An ATS with CRM (like Lever) focuses on software for tracking applicants and nurturing passive candidates, requiring you to handle recruiting yourself or hire separately. A recruiting tool combines the software with access to vetted recruiters who work as part of your team, giving you both tools and expert help in a single package.


### When should I consider switching from Lever to another solution?


If you’re facing high costs that strain your budget, struggling with limited reporting capabilities, or need recruiting expertise beyond just software, it’s worth assessing alternatives. Startups especially benefit from switching when they need faster setup, more flexibility, or want to avoid multi-year contracts.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing the Right ATS for Your Hiring Needs


Choosing the right ATS comes down to finding tools that support real hiring needs without adding layers that slow daily work. Lever offers notable capabilities, yet its pricing model and learning curve can leave teams looking for options with simpler access and stronger value. Many groups turn to Dover as a[Lever alternative](https://www.dover.com/) because it provides a free ATS, practical automation, and access to recruiting specialists who can step in when hiring surges. This mix helps small teams move quickly without locking into long contracts or dedicating large budgets to basic functions. By starting with software that removes friction and backing it with flexible support, your company can adapt to changing goals while keeping control of process and spend.
